steps.sop: The Software Engineer merges the approved PR in the source code/CI-CD repository; the review thread, approval records, and CI run URL are retained with the merge commit SHA and UTC timestamp for at least 12 months. Done when the merge completes with evidence intact.
steps.verify: Open the merged PR in the source code/CI-CD repository; pass if the merge commit SHA, approvals, resolved threads, and CI run URL are all retrievable from the work item link.

steps.title: Define the performance test plan and scenarios
steps.sop: The QA Analyst defines the test plan in Apache JMeter / k6 Performance Testing covering the high-traffic and latency-sensitive components in release scope (public APIs, quote/bind endpoints, batch ingestion), pinned to the specific service build/tag under test plus its direct downstream dependencies, with four scenarios: steady-state load, peak at 2x expected, 2-hour soak, and spike. Done when the plan names components, build SHA, and all four scenarios.
steps.verify: Open the test plan in Apache JMeter / k6 Performance Testing; pass if it lists the in-scope components, the exact build/tag, and all four scenario definitions.

steps.title: Link the campaign to the change ticket and CI build
steps.sop: The QA Analyst records the release change ticket (Jira release id / change record) and the CI pipeline run that produced the tested build on the campaign record. Done when both references are attached.
steps.verify: Open the campaign record; pass if it references the release change ticket and the producing CI pipeline run.

steps.title: Execute all scenarios against the tagged build
steps.sop: The QA Analyst executes the steady-state, 2x peak, 2-hour soak, and spike scenarios in Apache JMeter / k6 Performance Testing against the tagged build in the pre-production performance environment, before the go/no-go gate. Done when all four scenarios complete.
steps.verify: Open the run results in Apache JMeter / k6 Performance Testing; pass if results exist for all four scenarios executed against the correct build SHA in pre-production.

steps.title: Capture the full metric set per scenario
steps.sop: The Software Engineer confirms every scenario's report in Apache JMeter / k6 Performance Testing records p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput (req/s), error rate, and resource utilisation; results are not accepted until all fields are populated. Done when every scenario report is complete.
steps.verify: Open each scenario report in Apache JMeter / k6 Performance Testing; pass if p50/p95/p99, throughput, error rate, and resource utilisation are populated for all scenarios.

steps.title: Reconcile requests issued to responses recorded
steps.sop: The Backend Developer reconciles requests issued against responses recorded in Apache JMeter / k6 Performance Testing; the counts must agree within 0.1%, and any unaccounted requests are investigated and explained before the run is deemed valid. Done when the reconciliation passes or is explained.
steps.verify: Open the reconciliation in the run report; pass if issued vs recorded counts agree within 0.1% or every discrepancy has a documented explanation.

steps.title: Evaluate results against targets and baseline
steps.sop: The QA Analyst evaluates results in Apache JMeter / k6 Performance Testing against the pass thresholds — p95 <= 500 ms, p99 <= 1 s, error rate < 0.1% at target throughput — and against the prior release baseline, allowing no more than 5% p95 latency regression without a signed waiver. Done when every scenario is marked pass/fail.
steps.verify: Open the evaluation table; pass if each scenario shows the threshold comparison and baseline delta, with any regression over 5% explicitly flagged.

steps.title: Log target breaches as defects with disposition
steps.sop: The QA Analyst logs each scenario breaching a target as a defect (type Performance) with severity, owner, and disposition (fix / accept-with-waiver / block-release); a failure blocks the release gate, and a waiver requires an 'SDLC-Exception' ticket with a remediation plan and 10-business-day SLA. Done when every breach has a dispositioned defect.
steps.verify: Open the defects for the campaign; pass if every breached target has a defect with severity, owner, and disposition, and any waiver shows an approved 'SDLC-Exception' with remediation plan.

steps.title: Export the evidence keyed to the build SHA
steps.sop: The QA Analyst exports the test plan, load profile, raw result files, and dashboards from Apache JMeter / k6 Performance Testing to the CI artifact store, tagged with the build SHA and UTC run timestamp, retained for the release's audit window; results expire and must be re-run if the build SHA changes before deployment. Done when all artifacts are stored and keyed.
steps.verify: Open the CI artifact store entry; pass if plan, load profile, raw results, and dashboards are present, keyed to the tested build SHA with the UTC run timestamp.

steps.title: Capture QA Analyst sign-off on the performance report
steps.sop: The QA Analyst signs the performance report confirming all scenarios met latency/throughput/error targets with no regression over 5% (or that waivers are approved). Done when the signed report is stored with the campaign evidence.
steps.verify: Open the signed performance report in the CI artifact store; pass if it carries the QA Analyst's dated sign-off and matches the evaluation results.

steps.title: Confirm scan configurations are current and version-controlled
steps.sop: The Application Security Lead confirms the SAST rulesets, DAST scope, and authentication configs are version-controlled and current, with the config version referenced in SonarQube. Done when the active configs match the controlled versions.
steps.verify: Open the scan configuration in SonarQube; pass if the ruleset/config versions are referenced, current, and traceable to version control.

steps.title: Run SAST and SCA across the release repos
steps.sop: The Software Engineer runs SAST over all first-party source and SCA over all third-party dependencies for every service/repo in the release train in SonarQube, on every pull request and nightly. Done when current results exist for 100% of release repos.
steps.verify: Open the scan dashboard in SonarQube; pass if every release repo shows a SAST and SCA result from the current PR or nightly cycle.

steps.title: Run DAST against the staging deployment
steps.sop: The Application Security Lead runs DAST over the deployed application in the staging environment for each release candidate before promotion to production, covering every externally-reachable endpoint, with a full authenticated DAST at least monthly. Done when the release-candidate DAST report is produced.
steps.verify: Open the DAST report for the release candidate; pass if it covers all externally-reachable staging endpoints and a full authenticated scan is dated within the last month.

steps.title: Confirm detection with the known-vulnerable canary
steps.sop: The Application Security Lead includes a known-vulnerable canary in the scan population and confirms the scanners flag it in SonarQube. Done when the canary finding appears in the results.
steps.verify: Search the results in SonarQube for the canary component; pass only if its known vulnerability was detected and reported.

steps.title: Triage findings with complete records
steps.sop: The Application Security Lead triages each finding in SonarQube so it carries rule id/CWE, severity (CVSS), file/endpoint location, status, and remediation owner; false positives are suppressed with justification in the tool. Done when every open finding is complete and every suppression justified.
steps.verify: Sample open findings in SonarQube; pass if all five fields are populated on each and every suppressed finding shows a written justification.

steps.title: Reconcile critical and high findings to the backlog
steps.sop: The Software Engineer reconciles findings between the SonarQube dashboard and the tracking backlog: 100% of open critical/high findings must have a matching Jira ticket with counts matching exactly, under severity SLAs of critical 7 days, high 30, medium 90. Done when the reconciliation shows zero delta.
steps.verify: Compare SonarQube open critical/high counts to the tracking tickets; pass only if the counts match exactly and each ticket carries the correct severity SLA date.

steps.title: Enforce the release security gate
steps.sop: The Software Engineer confirms the CI security gate: 0 critical/high SAST or SCA findings unaddressed, no more than 5 medium findings and only with approved waivers, and no unremediated high-risk DAST issue; an un-waived critical/high blocks promotion, and risk acceptance requires an 'SDLC-Exception' ticket approved by the Application Security Lead with a dated remediation plan. Done when the gate is green or all exceptions are formally approved.
steps.verify: Open the security gate status in SonarQube; pass if the gate is green, or every blocking finding has an approved 'SDLC-Exception' with a dated remediation plan.

steps.title: Retain scan reports with the release record
steps.sop: The Software Engineer stores the SAST/DAST/SCA reports (SARIF + HTML) tagged with commit SHA, scan config version, and timestamp, retained 12 months and attached to the release change record. Done when the evidence set is attached.
steps.verify: Open the release change record; pass if SARIF and HTML reports are attached, tagged with commit SHA, config version, and timestamp.

steps.title: Capture Application Security Lead sign-off
steps.sop: The Application Security Lead records a dated sign-off confirming scans ran with current rulesets on the full scope and all critical/high findings are triaged, on the release evidence record. Done when the sign-off is recorded before release.
steps.verify: Open the release evidence record; pass if a dated Application Security Lead approval is present and predates the release promotion.

steps.title: Define the peak-condition scenario plan
steps.sop: The QA Analyst defines the load-test plan in k6 / Gatling Streaming Load Testing for the deployed stream job version in the staging streaming cluster, with three scenarios: sustained target rate, 2x burst, and a partition-rebalance during load. Done when the plan names the job version and all three scenarios.
steps.verify: Open the plan in k6 / Gatling Streaming Load Testing; pass if it pins the tagged stream job version and defines sustained, 2x burst, and rebalance scenarios.

steps.title: Link the run to the change ticket and CI build
steps.sop: The QA Analyst records the stream deployment change ticket and the CI pipeline run that built the tested stream job on the campaign record. Done when both references are attached.
steps.verify: Open the campaign record; pass if it references the deployment change ticket and the producing CI pipeline run.

steps.title: Execute the scenarios against the tagged job
steps.sop: The QA Analyst executes all three scenarios in k6 / Gatling Streaming Load Testing against the tagged stream job in the staging cluster before promotion. Done when all scenarios complete against the correct version.
steps.verify: Open the run results in k6 / Gatling Streaming Load Testing; pass if results exist for all three scenarios executed against the tagged job version.

steps.title: Capture the required metrics per run
steps.sop: The Data Engineer confirms each run in k6 / Gatling Streaming Load Testing records sustained events/sec, end-to-end latency (p95/p99), consumer lag, and dropped-message count; results are not accepted until all fields are populated. Done when every run report is complete.
steps.verify: Open each run report in k6 / Gatling Streaming Load Testing; pass if events/sec, p95/p99 latency, consumer lag, and dropped-message count are populated.

steps.title: Reconcile produced versus consumed messages
steps.sop: The Backend Developer reconciles messages produced against messages consumed at the target rate; message loss must be 0, and any gap between produced and committed offsets is investigated before a pass. Done when the reconciliation shows 0 loss or a resolved explanation.
steps.verify: Open the reconciliation in the run report; pass only if produced equals consumed with 0 loss and any offset gap has a documented resolution.

steps.title: Evaluate results against thresholds and baseline
steps.sop: The QA Analyst evaluates the runs against the pass criteria — sustains target events/sec with p99 latency <= 2 s, consumer lag draining to 0 within 60 s of burst end, 0 message loss — and against the prior baseline, allowing no more than 5% latency or lag regression without a documented waiver. Done when each scenario is marked pass/fail.
steps.verify: Open the evaluation; pass if each scenario shows the threshold results and baseline delta, with any regression over 5% flagged for waiver.

steps.title: Log breaches as defects with disposition
steps.sop: The QA Analyst logs any breach of latency or lag targets as a Jira defect with severity, owner, and disposition (tune / scale / block-release); a failure blocks promotion, and a waiver requires an 'SDLC-Exception' ticket with a 10-business-day remediation SLA. Done when every breach has a dispositioned defect.
steps.verify: Open the campaign defects; pass if every breached target has a defect with severity, owner, and disposition, and waivers show an approved 'SDLC-Exception'.

steps.title: Export evidence keyed to the build
steps.sop: The QA Analyst exports the load profile, throughput/latency dashboards, and consumer-lag charts from k6 / Gatling Streaming Load Testing to the CI artifact store with build SHA and UTC timestamp, retained for the release audit window; a re-run is required if the deployed artifact changes before promotion. Done when all artifacts are stored.
steps.verify: Open the CI artifact store entry; pass if load profile, dashboards, and lag charts are present, keyed to the build SHA with UTC timestamp.

steps.title: Capture QA Analyst sign-off on validated targets
steps.sop: The QA Analyst records a dated sign-off that throughput and latency targets are validated under peak conditions for the tagged job version. Done when the sign-off is stored with the campaign evidence.
steps.verify: Open the campaign evidence; pass if a dated QA Analyst sign-off is present and consistent with all-scenario pass results.

steps.title: Scope the jobs, topics, and operators
steps.sop: The Software Engineer documents the named stream-processing job(s) requiring exactly-once semantics: source topics, checkpointing config, transactional sink(s), and the windowing operators, in the Event streaming platform (Kafka/Confluent) job scope record. Done when all four elements are enumerated.
steps.verify: Open the job scope record; pass if it names the jobs, source topics, sinks, checkpoint config, and windowing operators in scope.

steps.title: Set the exactly-once processing guarantee
steps.sop: The Backend Developer sets processing.guarantee=exactly_once (or Flink checkpointing mode EXACTLY_ONCE) with a transactional/idempotent sink on each in-scope job configuration in the Event streaming platform (Kafka/Confluent); a missing setting is a config failure caught in CI. Done when every in-scope job runs with the EOS guarantee.
steps.verify: Inspect the running job configuration in the Event streaming platform (Kafka/Confluent); pass if the exactly-once guarantee and transactional/idempotent sink settings are active on every in-scope job.

steps.title: Define the watermark strategy and allowed lateness
steps.sop: The Software Engineer defines the watermark strategy and the allowed-lateness window on the windowing operators of each job in the Event streaming platform (Kafka/Confluent). Done when both are configured on every windowed operator.
steps.verify: Inspect the job configuration in the Event streaming platform (Kafka/Confluent); pass if each windowing operator shows a defined watermark strategy and an explicit allowed-lateness value.

steps.title: Route beyond-lateness events to the side-output/DLQ
steps.sop: The DevOps Engineer configures the side-output/dead-letter topic in the Event streaming platform (Kafka/Confluent) so events arriving beyond allowed lateness are written there and logged, with a reconciliation job reporting DLQ volume and disposition tracked to closure. Done when the routing and volume report are active.
steps.verify: Send a test event beyond the allowed-lateness window in the Event streaming platform (Kafka/Confluent); pass if it lands on the side-output/DLQ topic, is logged, and appears in the DLQ volume report.

steps.title: Run the duplicate-injection test
steps.sop: The Data Engineer runs a duplicate-injection test against the configured job in the Event streaming platform (Kafka/Confluent); the output record count must equal the distinct input event count with 0 duplicates. Done when the test passes.
steps.verify: Open the duplicate-injection test report; pass only if output count equals distinct input count with 0 duplicate records.

steps.title: Run the delayed-event test
steps.sop: The Data Engineer runs a delayed-event test in the Event streaming platform (Kafka/Confluent) confirming late events within the allowed-lateness window are counted in results and events beyond it are routed to the side-output/DLQ. Done when both behaviors are demonstrated.
steps.verify: Open the delayed-event test report; pass if within-lateness events appear in the output aggregates and beyond-lateness events appear only on the side-output/DLQ.

steps.title: Attach the semantics test report to the change
steps.sop: The Software Engineer attaches the exactly-once/late-arrival test report to the merge/change record, retained 12 months, noting that re-validation is required on any change to sink, checkpoint interval, or watermark policy. Done when the report is attached with the re-validation note.
steps.verify: Open the merge/change record; pass if the test report is attached, dated, and states the re-validation triggers.

steps.title: Capture Data Engineer sign-off on semantics behavior
steps.sop: The Data Engineer records a dated sign-off that exactly-once and late-arrival semantics behave as specified for the current release. Done when the sign-off is recorded with the test evidence.
steps.verify: Open the change record; pass if a dated Data Engineer approval is present and both test reports (duplicate-injection and delayed-event) show passes.

tasks.taskName: Configure pipeline DAG schedules and triggers

steps.title: Inventory the DAGs in scope as code
steps.sop: The Data Engineer inventories every DAG/workflow with a schedule or trigger owned by the team in the Data pipeline orchestrator (Airflow/Dagster/Prefect), confirming each is stored as code with the orchestrator framework version pinned. Done when the inventory matches the committed definitions.
steps.verify: Compare the active DAG list in the Data pipeline orchestrator (Airflow/Dagster/Prefect) to the committed definitions; pass if every DAG in scope is stored as code and inventoried.

steps.title: Define required configuration on every DAG
steps.sop: The Software Engineer defines on each DAG in the Data pipeline orchestrator (Airflow/Dagster/Prefect): schedule (cron/event), retry policy, timeout, SLA, upstream/downstream dependencies, and on-failure alert target; a DAG missing an SLA or alert target fails the config-lint gate. Done when the lint gate passes for all DAGs.
steps.verify: Run the config-lint check; pass only if every DAG shows all six fields populated and the lint gate is green.

steps.title: Tag tier-1 and high-impact DAGs
steps.sop: The Data Engineer tags any DAG whose late/failed run affects more than 1 downstream consumer or a financial close as 'tier-1' with a 15-minute alert threshold in the Data pipeline orchestrator (Airflow/Dagster/Prefect); schedule changes to DAGs feeding regulatory reporting or a downstream SLA are flagged high-impact and require a non-prod dry-run before apply. Done when all qualifying DAGs are tagged.
steps.verify: Filter DAGs in the Data pipeline orchestrator (Airflow/Dagster/Prefect) by downstream impact; pass if every qualifying DAG carries the 'tier-1' tag with a 15-minute alert threshold and high-impact flags are set.

steps.title: Validate changed DAGs in non-prod
steps.sop: The Data Engineer validates each changed or new DAG (typically 3-15 per release) in the non-prod Data pipeline orchestrator (Airflow/Dagster/Prefect) with representative trigger conditions: it must fire on its defined schedule/trigger, respect retry and timeout policy, and emit the SLA-breach alert on an injected delay. Done when all changed DAGs pass.
steps.verify: Open the non-prod run logs in the Data pipeline orchestrator (Airflow/Dagster/Prefect); pass only if every changed DAG fired on schedule, honored retry/timeout, and raised the SLA alert on the injected delay.

steps.title: Confirm validated runs land data in the warehouse
steps.sop: The Data Engineer confirms the validated non-prod DAG runs produced the expected output in the Enterprise data warehouse/lakehouse target tables. Done when each validated DAG's output is present and correct.
steps.verify: Query the target tables in the Enterprise data warehouse/lakehouse; pass if each validated DAG's run output is present with expected row counts.

steps.title: Apply the configuration to production under a change ticket
steps.sop: The Software Engineer applies the validated schedule/trigger configuration to production in the Data pipeline orchestrator (Airflow/Dagster/Prefect), captured in an ITSM change ticket recording the git SHA, timestamp, and effective dates, retained 3 years. Done when production config matches the approved change.
steps.verify: Open the change ticket; pass if it records the git SHA, apply timestamp, and effective dates, and the production DAG config matches the committed version.

steps.title: Confirm the orchestration-sync check shows no drift
steps.sop: The Software Engineer confirms the count of active DAGs in the Data pipeline orchestrator (Airflow/Dagster/Prefect) matches the count of DAG definitions committed in the repo; drift fails the 'orchestration-sync' CI check. Done when the sync check is green.
steps.verify: Open the 'orchestration-sync' CI check result; pass only if it is green with active DAG count equal to committed definition count.

steps.title: Log failures and missed SLAs with disposition
steps.sop: The Data Engineer raises schedule conflicts, missed SLAs, and failed runs as ITSM incidents with disposition (rescheduled / backfilled / accepted) recorded within the incident's SLA; a DAG failing validation is held from production and logged as a Jira 'SDLC-Exception' owned by the Data Engineer, remediated within 5 business days before re-promotion. Done when every failure has a dispositioned record.
steps.verify: Open the period's incidents and exceptions; pass if each failed run or missed SLA shows a disposition within SLA and held DAGs show an 'SDLC-Exception' with a 5-business-day remediation.

steps.title: Capture Data Engineer sign-off on the applied configuration
steps.sop: The Data Engineer records a dated approval on the change ticket confirming all release DAGs passed non-prod trigger/SLA validation and production matches the repo. Done when the sign-off is recorded.
steps.verify: Open the change ticket; pass if a dated Data Engineer approval is present with the orchestrator run logs and 'orchestration-sync' report attached.

steps.title: Raise the environment change ticket with scope
steps.sop: The Software Engineer raises a change ticket in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) defining the QA environments to provision for the release: SIT and UAT tiers, their compute/data stores, seeded masked test data, integration stubs/live endpoints, and test-team access, refreshed each release and reset after UAT sign-off. Done when the ticket documents the full scope.
steps.verify: Open the change ticket in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if it lists SIT and UAT tiers, data stores, test data, integration endpoints, and access requirements.

steps.title: Provision environments from version-controlled IaC
steps.sop: The DevOps Engineer provisions each environment in Terraform Cloud from version-controlled IaC, running plan then apply per environment. Done when apply completes for SIT and UAT.
steps.verify: Open the plan/apply logs in Terraform Cloud; pass if each environment shows a completed apply sourced from version-controlled IaC.

steps.title: Verify zero drift against the prod-parity baseline
steps.sop: The DevOps Engineer runs terraform plan in Terraform Cloud after apply; it must show 0 drift versus the prod-parity baseline, and the provisioned resource inventory must match the IaC plan output. Done when drift is 0.
steps.verify: Open the post-apply plan in Terraform Cloud; pass only if it reports 0 changes and the resource inventory reconciles to the plan output with 0 drift.

steps.title: Load masked test data to manifest counts
steps.sop: The Software Engineer loads the masked test dataset into each environment; seeded record counts must match the expected dataset manifest, and if unmasked PII is detected the load is halted, the dataset purged, and an 'SDLC-Exception' opened with a 24-hour remediation SLA. Done when counts reconcile and the PII scan is clean.
steps.verify: Compare seeded record counts to the dataset manifest; pass only if counts match with 0 delta and the PII scan reports no unmasked records.

steps.title: Run the post-provision smoke test
steps.sop: The QA Analyst runs the post-provision smoke test in each environment; an environment failing the smoke test is not released to QA. Done when the smoke test is green in SIT and UAT.
steps.verify: Open the smoke-test report; pass if all smoke checks are green for every provisioned environment.

steps.title: Grant test-team access
steps.sop: The DevOps Engineer grants the test team access to the provisioned environments and records the grants on the change ticket in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira). Done when all required testers have working access.
steps.verify: Open the access records on the change ticket in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if every required tester has a recorded, active grant.

steps.title: Attach the provisioning evidence to the change ticket
steps.sop: The Software Engineer links the IaC state, terraform plan/apply logs from Terraform Cloud, and the smoke-test report to the change ticket in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira), timestamped and retained 12 months. Done when all evidence is linked.
steps.verify: Open the change ticket in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if the IaC state, plan/apply logs, and smoke-test report are linked with timestamps.

steps.title: Log provisioning exceptions with disposition
steps.sop: The Software Engineer logs any provisioning failure or config drift on the change ticket in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) with a disposition; the environment stays blocked from QA use until drift equals 0, owner = Software Engineer, 3-business-day SLA. Done when every failure is logged and dispositioned.
steps.verify: Open the exception entries on the change ticket in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if each shows owner, disposition, and resolution within 3 business days, with no QA use before drift reached 0.

steps.title: Capture QA Analyst sign-off releasing environments to QA
steps.sop: The QA Analyst records a dated approval on the change ticket in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) confirming the environments are provisioned, drift-free, seeded, and smoke-tested for QA execution. Done when the sign-off is recorded.
steps.verify: Open the change ticket in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if a dated QA Analyst approval is present after green smoke tests and 0-drift confirmation.

steps.title: Pull the funding-check-pending queue
steps.sop: The Demand Manager filters the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) for every item in project 'DEMAND' with status 'Triage' and label 'funding-check-pending', covering the rolling 6-month planning horizon (current fiscal quarter plus next). Done when the queue is listed for the cycle.
steps.verify: Open the filter in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if it returns all 'Triage' items labeled 'funding-check-pending' and none outside that population.

steps.title: Validate required fields on each demand item
steps.sop: The Demand Manager checks each item in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) for non-null Funding Source, Approved Budget Amount greater than 0, Cost Center, Target PI, and Assigned Squad, with estimate points populated. Done when every progressing item has all fields valid.
steps.verify: Inspect the items in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if 100% of items progressing show all five fields populated with budget amount and capacity points greater than 0.

steps.title: Confirm funding against the FY plan line
steps.sop: The Demand Manager validates each item's funding in the PPM tool (Clarity/Planview/Jira Align) against the approved FY capital/opex plan line: remaining balance must be at least the approved amount, reconciled to the dollar, with the funding effective date inside the approved FY budget period. Done when the plan line ID and balance check are recorded per item.
steps.verify: Open the plan line in the PPM tool (Clarity/Planview/Jira Align); pass if the remaining balance covers the approved amount to the dollar and the effective date falls within the FY budget window.

steps.title: Confirm squad capacity for the target PI
steps.sop: The Resource Manager validates capacity in the PPM tool (Clarity/Planview/Jira Align) against the current PI capacity plan: the squad's available story points must be at least the item's estimate, and total committed demand for the PI must reconcile to available capacity within plus-or-minus 5%. Done when the capacity check is recorded per item.
steps.verify: Open the PI capacity view in the PPM tool (Clarity/Planview/Jira Align); pass if available points cover the estimate and committed demand is within 5% of squad capacity.

steps.title: Post the confirmation comment with evidence links
steps.sop: The Demand Manager posts a comment on the Jira demand item in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) recording the confirmed funding source, Clarity plan line ID, and confirmed squad capacity in points, with author and ISO-8601 timestamp, and links the comment and plan line in the item's 'Evidence' field. Done when the comment and links are in place.
steps.verify: Open the demand item in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if the confirmation comment shows funding source, plan line ID, capacity points, author, and ISO-8601 timestamp, and the 'Evidence' field links both.

steps.title: Block items failing the funding or capacity check
steps.sop: The Demand Manager moves any item failing either check to status 'Blocked-Funding' in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) with a comment stating the gap; the disposition is tracked to closure within 5 business days. Done when every failing item is blocked with the gap stated.
steps.verify: Filter 'Blocked-Funding' items in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if each shows the gap comment and a disposition dated within 5 business days.

steps.title: Escalate persistent failures via SDLC-Exception
steps.sop: The Demand Manager re-performs the failed check against the PPM tool (Clarity/Planview/Jira Align); if it still fails, raises a Jira 'SDLC-Exception' ticket in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) with a 10-business-day remediation SLA while the item stays in 'Blocked-Funding'. Done when persistent failures carry an exception ticket.
steps.verify: Open the exception tickets in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if each persistent failure shows the re-performed check and an 'SDLC-Exception' with a 10-business-day SLA.

steps.title: Capture Demand Manager sign-off on the cycle
steps.sop: The Demand Manager records a dated sign-off in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) confirming 100% of items progressed to analysis have a recorded funding-and-capacity confirmation with 0 unresolved exceptions. Done when the sign-off is recorded.
steps.verify: Open the cycle record in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if a dated Demand Manager approval is present and every progressed item carries its confirmation comment.

steps.title: Gather availability inputs for the sprint
steps.sop: The Scrum Master gathers each member's PTO (from the HR calendar snapshot taken on the planning date), ceremony load, on-call duty, and part-allocations covering the upcoming two-week sprint's working days. Done when inputs exist for every team member.
steps.verify: Review the availability inputs; pass if every member has PTO, ceremony, on-call, and allocation data dated to the planning-day HR calendar snapshot.

steps.title: Compute per-member capacity with the focus factor
steps.sop: The Software Engineer computes each member's capacity as working days x focus factor (typically 0.7-0.8, documented) minus PTO/ceremonies/on-call, so every team member has an entry. Done when all members have a computed capacity and the focus factor is documented.
steps.verify: Recompute a sample member's capacity; pass if the arithmetic matches, the focus factor used is documented, and no member lacks an entry.

steps.title: Record the capacity plan in the planning tool
steps.sop: The Scrum Master records the per-member and team capacity in the Jira capacity plan in Jira; Jira Align / Rally; Azure DevOps, timestamped at planning. Done when the capacity view is populated for Sprint <n>.
steps.verify: Open the capacity view in Jira; Jira Align / Rally; Azure DevOps; pass if every member's entry is present and the plan is timestamped at the planning session.

steps.title: Reconcile member capacity to the team total
steps.sop: The Scrum Master reconciles the sum of member capacities to the team total shown in the Jira capacity view in Jira; Jira Align / Rally; Azure DevOps. Done when the sum matches the total.
steps.verify: Sum the member entries in Jira; Jira Align / Rally; Azure DevOps; pass only if the sum equals the displayed team total.

steps.title: Check the commitment does not exceed capacity
steps.sop: The Product Owner and Scrum Master compare committed sprint points to computed capacity in Jira; Jira Align / Rally; Azure DevOps; committed points must be less than or equal to capacity with no over-commit. Done when the comparison is recorded.
steps.verify: Compare committed points to computed capacity in Jira; Jira Align / Rally; Azure DevOps; pass if committed is less than or equal to capacity.

steps.title: Flag shortfalls and record the action taken
steps.sop: The Scrum Master flags any capacity shortfall (over-commit or key-person absence) in the planning notes and either reduces scope with the Product Owner or escalates the dependency. Done when every shortfall shows the action taken.
steps.verify: Open the planning notes; pass if each flagged shortfall records the resolution: scope reduced, dependency escalated, or accepted with rationale.

steps.title: Capture Scrum Master sign-off on the capacity plan
steps.sop: The Scrum Master records a dated sign-off on the capacity plan in Jira; Jira Align / Rally; Azure DevOps confirming capacity for Sprint <n>. Done when the sign-off is recorded before the sprint starts.
steps.verify: Open the capacity plan in Jira; Jira Align / Rally; Azure DevOps; pass if a dated Scrum Master approval is present and predates the sprint start.

steps.title: Validate the candidate stories are ready
steps.sop: The Software Engineer checks every story proposed for the upcoming sprint in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira): each must have story points estimated, no unresolved blockers, and a defined acceptance criterion. Done when 100% of candidates pass or are removed.
steps.verify: Open the candidate set in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass only if 100% of committed stories show points, zero unresolved blockers, and an acceptance criterion.

steps.title: Compute capacity-adjusted velocity
steps.sop: The Scrum Master computes the rolling 3-sprint average velocity in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira), adjusted for PTO, ceremonies, and support load over exactly the upcoming sprint's working days as defined in Jira. Done when the calculation is recorded.
steps.verify: Open the recorded calculation; pass if it uses the last 3 sprints' velocity, applies the documented capacity adjustments, and covers the sprint's exact working days.

steps.title: Compare the commitment to the velocity band
steps.sop: The Software Engineer compares committed story points against capacity-adjusted velocity in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); the commitment must fall within 90-110%, with the delta shown in the sprint planning notes. Done when the comparison and delta are documented.
steps.verify: Open the planning notes; pass if the committed-vs-velocity delta is recorded and falls within the 90-110% band, or a documented exception exists.

steps.title: Negotiate descope for infeasible commitments
steps.sop: The Product Owner and Software Engineer negotiate descope in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) when the commitment exceeds the feasible band, recording which stories were deferred. Done when the revised commitment is feasible or the residual is escalated.
steps.verify: Open the planning record in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if descope decisions are recorded with the deferred stories named and the revised total re-checked against velocity.

steps.title: Log residual over-commitment as SDLC-Exception
steps.sop: The Scrum Master logs any commitment above 110% of capacity-adjusted velocity as a Jira 'SDLC-Exception' in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) with justification, owner = Scrum Master, Product Owner acknowledgement, and a same-sprint resolution SLA. Done when every over-commitment carries the exception.
steps.verify: Open the exceptions in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if each over-commitment shows justification, Scrum Master ownership, Product Owner acknowledgement, and the same-sprint SLA.

steps.title: Record the versioned planning note
steps.sop: The Software Engineer records the sprint planning note (capacity, velocity, commitment, delta) versioned and timestamped, linked from the sprint in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira), retained 24 months. Done when the note is linked from the sprint.
steps.verify: Open the sprint in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if the linked planning note shows capacity, velocity, commitment, version, and timestamp.

steps.title: Capture Scrum Master sign-off on feasibility
steps.sop: The Scrum Master records a dated sign-off on the planning note confirming the commitment is feasible (within 90-110% with all stories estimated and blocker-free) before the commitment is locked. Done when the sign-off predates sprint start.
steps.verify: Open the planning note; pass if a dated Scrum Master approval is present, dated before the sprint start, over a commitment within the feasible band or with logged exceptions.

steps.title: List required roles and environments from the charter
steps.sop: The Software Engineer lists every required role and every required environment (dev, test/QA, staging) for the initiative from the team charter on the mobilization readiness ticket in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira), during the Sprint 0 / mobilization window. Done when both lists with counts are recorded.
steps.verify: Open the readiness ticket in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if it lists all charter roles and the three environments with expected counts.

steps.title: Confirm a named person and access for every role
steps.sop: The Scrum Master confirms each required role is filled with a named person whose IAM access is granted, recording the roster with access grants on the readiness ticket in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira). Done when required roles equal confirmed assignments with 0 gaps.
steps.verify: Open the roster on the readiness ticket in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass only if every required role shows a named person and a recorded access grant.

steps.title: Verify each environment is provisioned and reachable
steps.sop: The DevOps Engineer verifies dev, test/QA, and staging are provisioned and reachable, recording the reachability checks on the readiness ticket in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira). Done when all three environments are verified healthy.
steps.verify: Open the environment checks on the readiness ticket in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if all three environments show a passed reachability check.

steps.title: Confirm a green pipeline in every environment
steps.sop: The DevOps Engineer runs the pipeline smoke tests for each environment in the source code/CI-CD repository. Done when dev, test/QA, and staging each show a green pipeline run.
steps.verify: Open the pipeline runs in the source code/CI-CD repository; pass only if each environment's smoke pipeline is green.

steps.title: Complete the readiness checklist with evidence
steps.sop: The Software Engineer ticks every readiness checklist field and saves the team roster and environment results with timestamp on the readiness ticket in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira). Done when the checklist is fully ticked with evidence attached.
steps.verify: Open the readiness ticket in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if all checklist fields are ticked and the roster and environment results are attached with timestamps.

steps.title: Log gaps as Mobilization-Blocker items
steps.sop: The Scrum Master logs any unfilled role or unavailable environment as a 'Mobilization-Blocker' item in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) with owner and target date; blockers open more than 5 business days are escalated beyond the team. Done when every gap has a blocker item.
steps.verify: Open 'Mobilization-Blocker' items in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if each gap has an owner and target date, and any item older than 5 business days shows an escalation.

steps.title: Gate Sprint 1 on 100% readiness
steps.sop: The Scrum Master confirms 100% readiness (all roles filled with access, all environments green) before Sprint 1 starts; otherwise the start is deferred or scope reduced, with the decision recorded on the readiness ticket in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira). Done when the gate decision is recorded.
steps.verify: Open the readiness ticket in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if readiness was 100% before Sprint 1, or a recorded defer/reduce-scope decision exists.

steps.title: Capture Scrum Master sign-off on mobilization readiness
steps.sop: The Scrum Master records a dated approval on the readiness ticket in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira) confirming team composition and environment readiness are both verified. Done when the sign-off is recorded.
steps.verify: Open the readiness ticket in the ITSM platform (ServiceNow/Jira); pass if a dated Scrum Master approval is present over the completed checklist.

steps.title: Compile the quarterly knowledge-gap list
steps.sop: The Software Engineer compiles the quarter's identified knowledge gaps (typically 15-30 items) on the quarterly knowledge-management plan page in Confluence, each assigned to a named SME. Done when every gap has a named SME.
steps.verify: Open the KM plan page in Confluence; pass if all identified gaps are listed and each is assigned to a named SME.

steps.title: Create a contribution record for each gap
steps.sop: The Software Engineer creates a contribution record in Confluence for each gap with topic, SME author, reviewer, target page/space, and due date. Done when all five fields are populated on every record.
steps.verify: Inspect the contribution records in Confluence; pass if 100% show topic, SME author, reviewer, target page/space, and due date.

steps.title: Maintain the SME delegation matrix
steps.sop: The Software Engineer maintains the delegation matrix in the KM space in Confluence naming, per topic area, the primary SME and a backup, so ownership is unambiguous when the primary is unavailable. Done when every topic area has a primary and backup.
steps.verify: Open the delegation matrix in Confluence; pass if every topic area on the plan names both a primary SME and a backup.

steps.title: Publish SME contributions to the target space
steps.sop: The Backend Developer and UI Developer (as assigned SMEs) author and publish their contributions to the target Confluence space by the due date. Done when each planned contribution is published.
steps.verify: Open the target pages in Confluence; pass if each planned contribution is published with the SME as the page author in version history.

steps.title: Obtain reviewer sign-off on every published page
steps.sop: The named reviewer records sign-off on each published page in Confluence; the KM tracking board blocks 'Done' until the page link and reviewer sign-off are present, and no page may be published without a named reviewer. Done when every published page carries a sign-off.
steps.verify: Inspect published pages in Confluence; pass only if 100% show a named reviewer sign-off — any published page without one is a fail.

steps.title: Link each contribution from the KM index
steps.sop: The Software Engineer links every completed contribution from the KM index in Confluence. Done when the index links all published pages.
steps.verify: Open the KM index in Confluence; pass if every published contribution is linked and the links resolve.

steps.title: Reconcile quarter totals at close
steps.sop: The Software Engineer reconciles the quarter in Confluence: planned contributions must equal captured + carried-over + dropped, with 0 items still in 'assigned' state past due at quarter close and at least 90% captured and peer-reviewed. Done when the reconciliation is recorded on the plan page.
steps.verify: Open the quarter-close reconciliation in Confluence; pass if planned = captured + carried-over + dropped, 0 overdue assigned items remain, and the captured-and-reviewed rate is >= 90%.

steps.title: Log deferrals and escalate blocked contributions
steps.sop: The Software Engineer records a disposition note in Confluence for any contribution an SME cannot complete this quarter (re-assigned or deferred); items unresolved after 2 quarters are escalated, and a business-critical gap is logged as an 'SDLC-Exception' with a 10-business-day remediation SLA. Done when every incomplete item has a disposition.
steps.verify: Open the disposition notes in Confluence; pass if every incomplete contribution shows re-assignment or deferral, 2-quarter items show escalation, and business-critical gaps show an exception with the 10-day SLA.

steps.title: Record quarter-close sign-off with the board export
steps.sop: The Software Engineer attaches the KM board export to the knowledge space in Confluence (retained 24 months) and records a dated quarter-close sign-off over the reconciliation. Done when the export and sign-off are both on the plan page.
steps.verify: Open the plan page in Confluence; pass if the KM board export is attached and a dated Software Engineer sign-off appears over the completed reconciliation.
